title: The Talking Mountain
subtitle: In this place, the mountains have a voice that is beyond the power of words.

items.text: The Talking Mountain

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: To save our comrades stranded in the mountains, we left the city by truck.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: A road was built outside the city, with our outposts and supply stations scattered along its route.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The locals often came down from the mountains to trade with our people.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Exchanging pretty stones for clothes, wool, and kisses for paper clips or old shoes—things that weren't worth much.

items.speaker: Interrogator II
items.text: Speak slowly, take your time.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: As our truck left the city, we passed a demolished tank by the side of the road.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Not long after, the driver said we were running low on fuel.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Lucky for us, a gas station was not far, guarded by troops like all the others.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: We hopped out and watched our truck slowly make its way over.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Everyone was relaxed and having a good time, chatting and laughing by the roadside, waiting for the truck to fill up and roll back around.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Why'd we all have to get out of the truck?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Because when the truck blows up, it's safer out here than it is in there.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: To our foes hiding in the mountains, destroying a vehicle can be more valuable than taking lives.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Don't scare the rookie, boss. It's a beautiful day, sunny and bright. Nothing bad is gonna happen.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Heh. It does feel good to stand here and soak up the sun, you might even grow a little taller.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Last month, our allies cleared out the nearby villages because they were supporting our enemies. So we have nothing to worry about, comrades. Relax and enjoy the sunshine!

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: We have been blessed with a peaceful day, haven't we, brother Aleksei? This is all thanks to your good fortune!

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Stay alert, Comrade Hassan. Keep your eyes on the mountains.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Among us, Aleksei was always the most on edge, while Hassan was the most relaxed.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: They didn't care whether I was a human or an arcanist. They only asked what unit I was in and where I served.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But not one of them even glanced at my Red-38! Hello? A broom of mass destruction over here, the ultimate ride! They weren't even the least bit curious about that?!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Imagine if they saw Zeno's arsenal, with flying carpets that breathe fire and ropes that seek out enemies, their jaws would hit the sand! Hah!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But none of that stuff is as good as my trusty broom!

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Before joining Zeno, I was begging on the streets of Juhalerat. Each day was either feast or famine, a roll of the dice. That was just how life was, haha!

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: But then one day, they came up to me and said, "Hey, kid, you want to join the army? We'll feed you! Three meals a day!" So I signed up.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Chatty Hassan, always so talkative.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Loyalty is easily bought over here. All it took was one pair of boots, two bowls of pilaf, and three square meals a day.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: After that, people from Zeno taught me to read and write, and told me all kinds of old stories.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: You know, just a friendly advice, be careful. It's okay to give gifts to the locals, but make sure you never take anything they give you.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: If you're lucky, it's poison; if not, it's a bomb.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Music boxes and dolls might just blow up in your hand.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Did I scare you? No need to be afraid, haha! Welcome to Juhalerat, Comrade Lilya! May you live a hundred years!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I've heard all of that before. Who do you think you're tryna spook?

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Yes, yes, you're a brave one! You are! By the way, where did you serve before?

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: She's like me, a student from Zeno.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Air Force Reserves.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: A fledgling falcon, ready to spread her wings! Did you fly here on this broomstick?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hassan caressed my Red-38, gently patting its metallic casing.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: This thing, you sit on it, and it really flies? That's the coolest thing ever, friend!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Want me to show you?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The curious crowd gathered around me, like spectators waiting for a show.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The clear skies, mountain roads, and the valleys between the peaks were like a perfect runway.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Go on, see if you really have the eyes of a hawk. Scout the mountains. We're counting on you.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Roger that, Commander!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Everyone cleared a path for me, and then my magnificent Red-38 and I took to the skies.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I heard cheers as I lifted off, or maybe they were gasps.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: There was nothing but mountains and trees out there, but it wasn't as barren as I thought. In the distance, a light was reflecting from the forest.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The shepherds and villagers in the mountains seemed to have noticed me, and looked my way from afar.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I waved, but I doubt they saw that.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: After circling the mountains, I returned to the ground to save fuel.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Ha! Ha! Can you take Hassan flying too? I've always wanted to see the sky!

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Hassan, man, you'd probably pee your pants, hahaha!

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: What're you talking about? Hassan's braver than a lion! What's a little flight to me? The lives that have fallen by my hand are more numerous than the sheep you've eaten for dinner!

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: That's not something to brag about, Comrade Hassan.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: You know, after the war, you can fly back to the Zeno Arms Academy with us on a special plane.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Yes! Of course I will! That's what you promised, right, boss?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Bertolt smiled and nodded, then checked his watch again. He seemed uneasy.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Sit next to me on the plane. I'll have a barf bag and stale crackers ready for your somersaulting stomach. Hah!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Laughter erupted from the crowd. Hassan grinned too, showing his yellow teeth and cackling so hard that even Bertolt cracked a smile.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Outside Juhalerat, the sun shone brightly as eagles glided across the blue sky.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The truck was parked at the gas station, with a few people going about their business. It seemed like an easy job.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: We really are lucky this time, all thanks to our little comrade, the goddess of luck! No mines or bombs, and no—
He spoke too soon.
A massive explosion erupts ahead, followed by two more in quick succession.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: That's the РПГ-8Д84! I'd recognize that sound anywhere! One rocket, three blasts.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: It's time for action, comrades!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The shock wave from the explosion of the truck and gas station left my ears ringing. I couldn't hear a thing.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But our comrades were quick to react. Hassan and two others had already found cover and started shooting up the hill.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Aleksei helped up a comrade who'd been knocked down by the blast, but thankfully they were a safe distance away.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: All in all, we lost a truck and a driver, nothing else.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But now we were caught with our pants down, and bullets started flying.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: I just had to go and jinx us!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: How did they get their hands on those things?

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: By the humps of a stubborn camel, how should I know? See that guy up there? Shoot back, boys! Open your eyes and aim, you sightless donkeys!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: We returned fire, but we were too far apart to hit each other. Despite the fierce exchange, none of us were injured in the slightest.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: About the РПГ-8Д84. It is an eighth generation portable rocket launcher, developed by the Zeno Arms Academy and issued in the fall of '84.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Believe me, these are some of the most intelligent rockets you'll ever see.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Amidst the deafening roars of wind and screeching, these explosives never fail to find their target.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I've played with these back at the academy. Powerful stuff, but luckily they're one-offs, and each one is a pain to cultivate.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But seriously, how the hell did the enemy get their hands on those things?

items.speaker: Interrogator II
items.text: So, are you saying that Zeno's arcanum weapons have fallen into enemy hands?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Good question. I wonder what really happened, comrade.

items.speaker: Interrogator II
items.text: We'll make a note of that.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: There was more. They all had Zeno uniforms as well.

items.speaker: Interrogator II
items.text: Hm. We recently shipped a new batch of uniforms to the front lines, as recorded by the logistics department.

items.speaker: Interrogator II
items.text: Some units have temporarily recruited local personnel to join their auxiliary forces. They needed Zeno's uniforms.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: A new batch of uniforms? No, that doesn't make sense. Hassan was still wearing his own clothes, and so were a bunch of other comrades!
Hearing this, the interrogator turns to the clerk, who nods in understanding.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: They retreated, and the shooting stopped.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Is anyone hurt?

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Boss? All the radio equipment were on the truck, but now they're gone.
The officer grimaces as he watches the smoke disperse. The truck and surrounding buildings continue to burn uncontrollably in the distance.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: The explosion was far from us, sir. The driver and the comrades at the gas station are gone, but our people here are unharmed.
The soldiers regroup, the most unfortunate among them sporting only a scratch on his arm.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: The good news is we survived unscathed. The bad news is we've now lost contact with the trapped party.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Bertolt forgot that he still had me.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Was the distress signal on a military channel?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Yes, an encrypted one. Do you have a plan, little falcon chick?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The experimental navigation radar ПВ-1182, a new gadget devised by Zeno's arcanists. Let's give it a try, it should be able to pick up a signal.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The creatures in the radar are highly trained. Certain frequencies can activate their dormant minds, prompting them to react accordingly.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Let me see that.
The soldiers begin to murmur at the mention of arcanists.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: There it is! But what happened? Why has the signal stopped in place?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: It might be unstable. It's still a prototype, after all.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Well, it's better than nothing.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: We were fortunate to have you here, Comrade Lilya!

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: But we no longer have a vehicle.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: If you don't have wheels, use your legs! Are you scared, brother Aleksei? Our people have been traversing these mountains for thousands of years!

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: He's right. Let's go. We'll follow where this thing goes.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: So off we went, toward the billowing smoke of the gas station.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The atmosphere had changed. There were no more jokes or laughter, just pairs of watchful soldiers, their eyes fixed on the hills.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: There's trees on that hill there. Maybe people there too.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: I wasn't wrong, comrade, we really are lucky to be alive.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Let me give you some advice. I know it's going to sound morbid, but you'd best keep a bullet for yourself, little comrade.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I'd rather jam my last bullet up an enemy's nostril.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Hahaha! But seriously, don't get caught alive, or you'll wish you'd died.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Bullets are merciful things! A bang, and you're gone, no pain at all! I've seen way too many soldiers in the infirmary, wailing in pain.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: I remember the missing limbs, such a pitiful sight. Lying in bed, calling out names, crying for their mothers.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I noticed a glimmer of tears in his eyes, but he quickly composed himself and burst into a mischievous laughter.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Those fiends torture their captives with blades coated in poison. I hear they have skilled arcanists who use cruel arts to leave their victims unable to live or die.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: For us here, blood is thicker than water. If someone hurts your family, you have to seek vengeance at any cost.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: You afraid yet? Ha, even the city isn't safe! Just remember, my young friend, never take anything from someone you don't know.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Even a lighter—press it and boom! Blow you to bits.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Get lost with your scare tactics, you've already told me that!

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Believe it or not, your choice.
The old soldier shrugs and pulls a handful of roasted beans from his pocket.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Want some? They may be cold, but they're still good. My wife fried them with salt! They're tasty!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: So there we were, a group of survivors, nibbling on chickpeas as we continued on our way.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Just a few beans is enough, indulge in too many and you'll be tooting like a tuba! Haha!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: As we passed the remains of the gas station, we all instinctively covered our faces from the thick, black smoke.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: We did not have the time to mourn.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Maybe there are still survivors.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Impossible, absolutely impossible. Nothing could have survived such an explosion. You would have to be some kind of monster!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But Aleksei did find a survivor.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Though she wasn't one of ours.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Look over there! I think I see someone!

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Aleksei!
Aleksei sprints ahead, too fast to be stopped. Bertolt quickly signals to follow.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Are you alright, miss?
The woman lies on the ground, eyes wide with terror. Her calf is cut by broken stones, bleeding profusely.
She looks like a frightened lamb, with a flock of unfortunate real lambs lying next to her, none spared by the explosion.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: You're hurt. Stay calm, I'll take care of it.
Aleksei crouches down, pulls out a first aid kit, and carefully tends to the woman's wounds.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: The disinfectant will sting a bit, but don't worry, I'll stop the bleeding first. Your injury is manageable, I've practiced this at the academy before.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: I think I see blood.
Aleksei kneels beside her, gently cleansing the wound and using precious cotton swabs to apply medicine before carefully wrapping it in a bandage.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: As we caught up with Aleksei and approached the scene, the woman became even more frightened at the sight of armed soldiers.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: She's from the hills.
When Hassan sees the woman in local dress, he unslings his rifle, loads it, and points it at her.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: What are you even doing? She doesn't have a gun! And she's hurt!
Aleksei jumps up and stands in front of the gun, using his own body to shield the frightened woman behind him.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: She comes from the hills, brother! There's a good chance she's a spy for "them"!

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Hassan, please! She's just a simple herder caught up in this terrible war! She's injured and defenseless!

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Are you out of your mind?! Think, brother Aleksei! Whatever is in your box is all that we have left!
The explosion had taken their truck, driver, radio equipment, and all their first aid supplies.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Listen to yourself! Are you telling me to leave her here to die? Just walk past a wounded lady on the roadside like she isn't even there?

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: She could just be a herder passing through to trade, and now her sheep are gone, all thanks to that d**n explosion!

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: There are herbs in the hills that can stop bleeding, and my ancestors have been using them for centuries. She's a hill person, she can take care of herself.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Do you really think she can survive through the hills with that injured leg?

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: #@&$! Why do you have to be such a crazy do-gooder, Aleksei?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: They were at each other's throats, but I didn't think Aleksei was wrong at the time.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Bertolt stepped in to break it up.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: That's enough. I believe this lady can find her way home now. We have other matters to attend to.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Time is ticking, comrades. Our fellow soldiers in the cave are still waiting for us.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: I'm not sure if we should leave a loose end like this, boss. What if one of her family members is an enemy of ours?

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Did you just say loose end? It'll have to be over my dead body, Hassan!

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: That's enough. Put away your gun, Hassan. And Aleksei, step away from her. Pack up the kit and medicine.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: She's a victim just like us, nearly killed in the attack. Let's leave it at that.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: I can only hope you're right.
Hassan sighs and slings his rifle back over his shoulder.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: If we were in the time of Nader Shah, our brother Aleksei would have been a great knight.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: But now, your kindness just might get us killed, Aleksei.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: And your lack of empathy is killing Zeno and its future here, Hassan.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: After that, we continued on our way.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Aleksei followed closely behind Hassan, glancing back every few steps until the woman limped out of sight and into the mountains. Only then did he seem to relax.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Our Aleksei is a good man, maybe even better than some of the other good men I know.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hassan, on the other hand, was reliable and experienced. I couldn't help but wonder what he had been through.
TO BE CONTINUED…
